These spikes are most prominent around its neck, forming a jagged mane and dwarfing its comparatively small head, which is vulpine in appearance. Its tail is also completely covered and becomes wider towards the end. Its hind legs are short with three-toed feet ending in barbed claws. Contrasting this, Firakai's gauntlet-like forelegs are significantly longer and bulkier, floating detached from the rest of the creature's body. There are five jagged claws positioned radially around the palm, resembling a five-pointed star when its fingers are splayed. Smoke billows out of the opposite end of each forelimb, as well as from the end of Firakai's mane a tail. By default, the creature is colored bright yellow, orange, red, and white with prominent ruddy brown accents. Its smoke is also white by default. Males have three extra floating spikes on their backs. Females have two extra floating spikes on their hind legs. They are omnivores. Firakai is a dog-like creature with eyes that sparkle like exploding stars, brimming with insatiable curiosity and boundless energy. Its tail is a cascade of sparkling smoke, joyously wagging tails of glorious embers.

entries.name: Flamerir
entries.content: Flamerir is a unique creature composed entirely of elemental raging fire, with long, flame-like structures brimming and spewing-like across its body. It bears some resemblance to the Pliohippus, an extinct horse genus deriving from the Late Miocene era, as well as resembling modern ponies and dwarf horses. Its primary colors transition from dark velvet red at the head to orange at the torso, and then to yellow at the tail. Its short, mane-like flames and underside of the neck are also yellow. The creature has a small head with pupil-less yellow eyes, a somewhat thick neck, and a long, skinny body. Its head also has flame-like structures resembling reindeer antlers. Its wings and small burst of flame-like structures are seen disconnected from its body, floating in place. Flamerir's front legs are more muscular than the back legs, with hooves similar to those of modern horses. Short flame-like structures protrude from the back of the creature's legs, seen between the pastern and forearm/stifle. Also, its long tail is reminiscent of a combusting flame. Males have two additional pairs of short, flame-like structures on their heads, resembling horns. They are carnivores. This creature is flame itself. Flamerir have no flesh, and can disappear at any moment from lack of oxygen. Water is very deadly for these creatures. Flamerir sets all alight when on land, so it prefers to stay in the air. Flamerirs are quite calm and try their best to not hurt the nature around them.

entries.name: Fleuralis
entries.content:
With button eyes, a big mane, and two long, striped horns that have sickle-shaped tips, the Fleuralis is a plush chimera (without any goat components). They have three dull spikes in a row running down their back and two tiny flightless wings. Fleuralis also have a lengthy tail with two additional spikes before the tip and a little, snake-like "head" on the end. The snake head also has a lengthy set of teeth and a big horn on its nose. Additionally, Fleuralis has a small circular bell against its throat that appears to be fastened by a ribbon around its lower jaw. Males have round bird-like wings on their backs. Females have sharp bat-like wings on their backs. They are omnivores. A stitched together looking mostly-feline with a few hints at a more reptilian lifestyle. Both parts cat and reptile seem to enjoy long hours basking and soaking up sunlight. Though Fleauralis are primarily docile, feeding on mostly gourds and berries, they will scavenge for carrion when food is bare.
- Fleuralis are basically mimic-carnivores, but are omnivorous in reality.
- The only thing that portrays this is their voice, which is goat-like.
- They'll eat just about anything they can get their paws on, including maybe things that they should or shouldn't eat, though it could actually be to aid digestion.

entries.name: Flickaflie
entries.content:
The Flickaflie has a moth-like appearance, with three fur-covered legs on either side of its body, big antennae and eyes, along with a set of pointed green wings bearing large holes in them. The Flickaflie also has two green glowing bulbs, seen at the end of its antenna and abdomen. Its wings and antennae take up most of its body compared to its small head, which bears a pointed nose. Its natural colors consist of a palette of black, grey, white, and green. They are herbivores. Flickaflie live simple lives, wanting nothing more than to follow the glow on their own lamps forever. They tend to live near food sources as their young grow quickly and need lots of food to satiate their large appetite.
- The lamps which adorn Flickaflie's heads attract them so much that they will follow it perpetually, never realizing that they must eat or drink.
- For others, the warm glow of their lamps brings peace to those who encounter it.
- Sometimes, Flickaflie bump into each other while flying, which causes more of them to join together and make a blinding flash of light, nearly impossible to look at.
- Flickaflie shed a lot of small scales that make up their fur, producing long trails of dust. They must wipe their eyes often as their own scales tend to accumulate on them.
- Flickaflie usually lay eggs underneath the leaves of large trees, and their offspring hatch as small, fuzzy worms.
- A group of Flickaflie are referred to as a 'Flickaflutter'.

entries.name: Flipli
entries.content: The Flipli is a small, round creature resembling a non-translucent water flea. Its default colors include blues and pinks, with the main body being mostly dark navy blue on top and pink underneath that fades into purple. It has two round blue eyes, a protruding snout, two pairs of whisker-like appendages, and a third pair of longer appendages ending in small bulbs, with another long pair above each eye. Bioluminescent dots are arranged in six vertical lines under its body, starting as light blue and fading into purple, capable of switching up to three colors when moving, in an up-down, front-back change wave pattern. Its back features thick swirly markings that begin as purple on top of its head and transition to a light blue swirl at each side of its body. Purple square-shaped markings are seen near the head and below the swirls, and rectangle-shaped markings lower down its back. The Flipli has three pairs of dark navy blue limbs situated lower down its body, each with three bioluminescent dots; the first pair has three light blue stubs for fingers, while the other pairs resemble flippers with a structure, similar in appearance to the fingers, at the ends. Additionally, its body ends in a short, narrow tail-like tip. Males have small tufts of fur or a fin on their upper back. They are herbivores. Flipli are round and small creatures that communicate through their lights in the depths of the ocean. On the brightest nights of the year, millions gather near the surface to creating a spectacular underwater light show.

entries.name: Flixlit
entries.content:
The Flixlit is a multi-winged wyvern creature with two pairs of sharp-pointed wings and a single pair of legs, which are hidden underneath the second pair of wings. It has golden accents lining its back and wings. Thin, feather-like blades protrude from the tip of its forewings and the midsection of its hind wings. In its jaws is a long yellow tongue. Thin shards float around the creature's head, neck, and the base of its tail, while 3 ring-like structures float around its tail. Males have an extra pair of floating shards on top their heads. Females have additional floating shards around their tails. They are herbivores. Flixlit are tiny playful fliers that skim Sonaria's oceans and light up the skies. Covered in glimmering star fragments, they leave bright golden trails wherever they fly. Some say that Flixlit actually came from the stars as curious visitors from another time.
- The Flixlit is "as dumb as a brick".
- Essentially glitter-covered seagulls at heart.

entries.name: Fluren
entries.content: The Fluren is a small dromaeosaurid-like creature covered in many leafy frills with vein-like structures. Larger frills adorn its head, while leafy frills resembling fins run down its neck, back, and the underside of the tail, which helps with maneuverability. Its long, thin tail also ends with a leafy fin, presumably acting as a rudder of sorts. Its long arms have leafy feathers, almost like wings, despite being flightless, and are used to slow down its descent while jumping, similar to dromaeosaurids and modern day birds. The Fluren's head features a few stem-like tendrils with small, bulb-like bioluminescent organs at the tips, with two pairs extending above the eyes and two longer pairs behind the jaw. More of these tendrils can be seen at the thighs, base of the tail, and lower down the tail. The Fluren has small eyes, no teeth, and its jaw structure forms somewhat of a downward drooping beak, accompanied by a long chin. Its back is lined with presumably thin armor plates, which also appear on its arms. It has long legs that support it for running long distances and performing high jumps, and feathers covering the thighs. Also, its feet are bird-like, with toes arranged in an anisodactyl formation. In general, its whole body resembles that of a raptor-shaped stick/leaf insect. Males have extra stem-like tendrils extending from the snout, each with bulb-like bioluminescent tips. Females have short, additional leaf-like frills around their head. They are photovores, which means they only need water and sunlight to survive. Fluren is a very timid creature, they spend most of their time hiding in foliage and trees. They are very good climbers, and will use it to escape predators.

entries.name: Frigiboa
entries.content: The Frigiboa is a six-legged, silverfish or isopod-like creature with a resemblance to its distant relative Militrua. It has plates on its back that extend along its tail, which ends in a pair of cerci (paired appendages at the end of the abdomen), and smaller appendages resembling wings fall behind its legs. Its head is round, with a pair of big eyes decorated with glowing plates resembling cartoony eyelashes, and a smaller pair of diamond-shaped ocellus. It has two pairs of antennae sprouting from its head, both ending with a wispy tip, with the second pair looking like whiskers sprouting from above its eyes. It seems to be heavily armored and has a color palette consisting of light browns and blues. Males present spike-like decorations at the end of their secondary coat plates on their torso and third leg pair wing-like appendages. Females present leafy/lichen-like decorations near the tip of their antennae and cerci. They are omnivores. Frigiboa are resilient insects that can be born from the thousands of dormant eggs that lay present in Sonaria's tundra. In the winter, they shed pieces of their cone like hides, fueling plant growth throughout the seasons in the harsh cold.

entries.name: Frigilinx
entries.content: The Frigilinx is a quadrupedal creature somewhat akin to a pangolin. It's covered in a light blue/purple/white plating that appear to be made of ice. Its arms are disproportionally large, especially when compared with its stout hind legs. The ice spikes that appear starting at its elbows and end at its wrists help the creature's arms to appear bigger than they really are. Ice plating swoops out at the end of its tail, adorned with small icicles much like the ones under its chin and narrow head. Males have a horn on their snout. They are herbivores. Frigilinx are timid, peaceful creature who reside in cold snow holes and prefer to remain hidden. Its powerful claws play a crucial role in both digging and combat.

entries.name: Furnilixii
entries.content: The Furnilixii is a quadrupedal flower-like creature with a stout body, and a huge, bulbous tail with a narrow tip, resembling an insect's abdomen. Its default colors consist of different shades of green and pink. It has large round eyes with hot pink eyeliner, a somewhat pig-like snout with two nostrils, and small, almost triangular ears. Its head also features four white spots on each cheek, a green spot above each eye, and short hot pink hair with bangs. The Furnilixii's somewhat long, thick neck is surrounded by enormous light pink petals that splay outward, with three pairs of petals arranged in a linear fashion underneath its neck, lower down. More petals can be seen covering the top of its tail in shades of hot and light pink colors. Large leaves grow behind its neck petals, at the base of its tail, and three-quarters down the tail. A pair of stamen-like structures protrude from atop its head and two pairs on top its neck and three pairs underneath. It also has a pair of longer, stamen/antenna-like structures on its head and two pairs extending backward alongside the leaves by its neck. Additionally, the Furnilixii has five toes on each foot, and bumpy structures on its legs, the underside of its torso, and its tail. Females have additional stamen-like structures on top of their tails. They are photovores, which means they only need water and sunlight to survive. Despite their innocent looks and gorgeous applea, these creatures have malicious intent to annoy anyone in their path. Their nimble movement and unpredictable patterns make them hard to catch and they can even detatch their own tails for a diversion.

entries.name: Fyluf
entries.content: The Fyluf has a small, pigeon/dove-like body with clumps of feathers situated on the back of the head, with a curved head and large tail feathers, and wide, bright eyes. The body is decorated with simple markings that consist of pink, white, yellow, and almost red-ish colors. It has bulky legs, resembling those of a hawk or owl. Due to its appearance and status as a Valentines Day creature, Fyluf may also draw inspiration from lovebirds and doves for their history of relating to the topic of love and tranquility. Males have two colorful crests on their heads. Females have three feathers on their backs. They are herbivores. Fyluf are creatures with an overwhelming cuteness about them. This often causes creatures to regret attacking them. Fyluf also are unable to fly due to their weight.

entries.name: Fyranili
entries.content:
Fyranili is a bipedal creature which resembles a dromaeosaurid in build and posture. Parts of its limbs, neck, head, and the base of its tail are covered in leafy feathering, and there are several large pepper-shaped protrusions jutting from its shoulders, wrists, ankles, back, and the "leaves" on its tail. Both of its horns are similarly thick and pepper-like in appearance, but each feature a small prong. Fyranili's tail also shares this resemblance to a chili pepper, and it is thicker and longer than the rest of the creature's body. The tail is covered in short barbs on both the dorsal and ventral side, and it ends in a sharp, slightly curled point like a bee's stinger. Both of Fyranili's four-fingered hands have a noticeable "thumb" claw and its theropod feet feature curved sickle-shaped claws. Its teeth protrude from the outside of its mouth and line the upper jaw exclusively. Small spots shaped like pepper seeds are scattered in rows of three on Fyranili's sides. By default, the creature features fiery shades of red, orange, and yellow, with dark green feathering and sparse white. Females have an additional pair of downwards-pointing pepper horns. They are photocarnivores, meaning they eat meat and don't need water to survive. Fyranili mutated from Molteno pepper, a playful yet hot-temper creature. Often lurks around the dry forest of Sonaria in groups. With their excellent teamwork, they can effortlessly take down any creatures that are much larger than themselves.
- Despite being aggressive predators, trying to be friends with these furious creatures might be easier than you think. They love challenging other creatures into a "Hot-spicy" challenge where they'll give you a Molteno pepper for you to consume, and if you're able to endure the incredible hotness of the pepper, they will forever be your friend.
- The Molteno pepper is a rare pepper that has an incredibly spicy flavor, with a Scoville scale of 6.3 million, as hot as an erupting volcano. Consumption could cause the consumer to suffer from burns for hours.
- Fyranili hunt other creatures mostly for fun, they show no mercy when it comes to killing due to their hot temper.
- They are very protective of their pack and friends. They do not let anyone who hurts their allies get away easily.

entries.name: Galeostra
entries.content:
Galeostra is a six-limbed gastropod creature with a very strong resemblance to its inspiration, the Glaucus atlanticus. As such, it has six main "leg" appendages, from which multiple cerata and fingerlike appendages stem, and smaller versions of these tendrils protruding from the snout and tail. Unlike its inspiration, its longest tendrils do not protrude from the extremities, but from the shoulders and base of the tail. Its ventral area and tail are not only coated with a slime-like effect, created by reversing visible faces on some parts, but are also decorated with a dotted-star bioluminescence. They are herbivores. Galeostra are calm beasts, venturing around Sonaria's oceans. Very rarely are they seen and most often during an aurora or while a meteor shower is happening. Despite being big they have fragile skin and rely on a potent poison to protect themselves; Even just touching them can cause severe irritation. 
- Galeostra are neutral creatures and couldn't care less about the shoals of fish they attract with their flickering lights.
- Galeostra are not great parents and often lose their babies while traveling. Despite this, many of the babies end up making it to adulthood.
- Galeostra are surprisingly good at breaching and are often mistaken for shooting stars. They can flicker their lights in patterns and even communicate with each other using this method.
- The second Galeostra are born they start eating a wide variety of poisonous flora, even though it provides little to no sustenance for them.
- They like to wander the twilight zone of Sonaria's oceans in search of some of their favorite food.

entries.name: Galiryn
entries.content: The Galiryn possesses a sleek, muscular body reminiscent of large cats, combined with draconic features. It has a feline-like head, yellow eyes with slit pupils that exude intelligence and alertness, sharp teeth, lion-like ears, and a pair of horns, each adorned with a yellow ring-like object. Long fur covers its cheeks and atop its long neck, with a yellow accessory—similar to the ones on its horns—tying the fur on each side of its cheeks. Additional fur covers its upper body and atop the lower torso, stopping at the base of the tail. The Galiryn's broad, feathered wings are equipped with sharp-clawed "thumbs". Both its front and back limbs have four toes, each with sharp claws; the back inner claws resemble those of a raptor. Additionally, its primary coloration includes dark grays and blacks, with accents of red and white. Beneath its vibrant fur is dark, scaly skin, which can be seen at its lower arms, lower torso, hind legs, and its long, crocodile-like tail. They are carnivores. Galiryn are lively and intelligent feline-like creatures with draconic elements. Galiryn are well adapted to suit nearly any environment they may face, whether as low as the sea or as high as the sky. These efficient night hunters escape detection from their prey with their wits combined with dark scales and cloaking wings.

entries.name: Galtekron
entries.content: The Galtekron is a thin and bony bird-like creature that resembles the Quetzalcoatlus. On its head is a large spike that juts from its chin as well as some plates that line its lower jaw. Along its neck, which makes up the majority of the Galtekron's length, are four curved rectangular spines that get thicker as they approach the base of the neck. More curved spines can be seen jutting from the chest and back of the Galtekron. The Galtekron has short arms along with rather long fingers which bear long, curved claws. Attached to the arm and 'pinky' of the Galtekron is the webbing for its wings, which split off into three different pieces towards the tip of the wing. Lastly, it seems to have a thin, fan-like tail. Males have a single fin extending from the start of their neck to their chin. They are carnivores. Galtekron are calm and gentle scavengers that spend most of their lives aloft. They don’t pay mind to directions and tend to let air currents push them along. In the moments they aren’t flying, they hook themselves onto walls to rest. To other creatures, seeing Galtekrons flying is a sign of clear skies and good weather.

entries.name: Garra Warden
entries.content: The Garra Warden is a theropod-shaped creature with an overall dark red and bone white colors with an almost zombie-like and skeletal appearance, with markings and features that suggest exposed bone, bare flesh, and muscular tissue. It has two pairs of long arms, each with lengthy, curvy claws and markings that resemble the hand and arm skeletal structures. It has a protruding snout and a chin which protrudes even more. Its mouth has white, long, curled teeth that point towards its skull, and a long, red tongue. The back of its head has four thin, curled bony horns. There is a hood of skin lined with sharp protrusions that resembles the hoods seen on certain snake species like cobras, followed by a similar flap covering its rump and leading down to a long tail. Males have multiple spikes on their heads. They are herbivores. The Garra Warden reaps havoc upon those who oppose it every eclipse as the chaos that fuels it is spent. A mysterious and ominous presence, one of its many names, "Mors'vuhk" is inscribed in runes across Sonaria and it is worshipped by many as the true guardian of the dead. Although small in size, do not underestimate this Warden, as that will be your last mistake...

entries.name: Geogoff
entries.content:
The Geogoff is an armored quadruped with quills sprouting from its back and face. It has a large bushy tail, and paws made for digging. It is colored with shades of brown and light blue. It looks like a combination of a sloth and a mole in stature and appearance. It also has dim-slit eyes and sharp teeth. Males have a beard-like formation under their chin. They are omnivores. Geogoff are primarily terraforming creatures and use their quills to navigate, as they are blind. They make homes in warm soil or find damp caves to hide out in. Their bodies rely on warmth as there is no fur to cover their bodies.
- Geogoff will eat anything and everything, including tree roots. However, they typically only chew on tree roots with the express purpose of filing down their teeth.
- Geogoff will touch noses with others of their kind in order to communicate, much like how bees communicate in a hive.
- A Geogoff's natural instinct is to start digging, and if one has not dug in a couple days, they will start to become anxious.
- Due to this, Geogoff tunnels can span up to hundreds of miles.
- While a Geogoff's front paws are strong and muscular and powerful enough to cause heavy damage to foes, they would rather use these paws to dig.

entries.name: Geoptxina
entries.content:
The Geoptxina is stout quadrupedal creature which bears a large resemblance to real life tortoises. It has a square-ish head with a sharp beak and no teeth. Its eyebrow ridge and the sides of its neck are lined with wide spikes. The Geoptxina has a uniquely shaped shell in that it creates a triangular shape when viewed from the front or a three-fourths angle. The "scutes" of its shell start from the creatures tail up to its shoulders, and they curve forward in such a way where there is an overhang on the front of each scute. Underneath each overhang is a crystalline texture, making the Geoptxina's shell resemble a geode when viewed at the right angles. The creature has a mid-sized tail, which has a heavy club on its tail tip. Males have spikes along the sides of their jaw. They are herbivores. Geoptxinas are professional nap takers. They love to spend their time alone, undisturbed in the darkness, where their geode patterns tingle and shine like a starry night. They can get to be highly territorial and not something easy to fight off, especially with their sharp shell.
- They are rather sleepy all the time, so they stay long periods of time just resting in shallow waters in summer and inside caves on winter immobile.
- Geoptxinas store energy to walk many kilometers and never get tired.
- Baby Geoptxinas (called pebbles) are very energetic, practicing their head-butting against bigger and taller creatures' legs.
- Babies are also born mature enough to be on their own, so they are independent on the get go.
- They maintain their hearts to a slow but powerful rhythm, and their blood is mesothermic. Very adaptable to different temperatures, but prefer warmth.
- If smaller creatures are looking for shelter, Geoptxinas don't mind having them hide in the shell as long as they are not annoying, even defending the little creatures from predators.
- They can be rather territorial and try scaring away their own kin or anything bigger than themselves.
- They get to live up to 300 years, and are not that smart.
- Melons, gourds and any big, juicy fruit are their favorite meals.
- If one were to look long enough, the geode crystals in the shell shimmer and glow with mild bioluminescence that serves to mesmerize and calm down.

entries.name: Geortharoc
entries.content: The Geortharoc is a huge, bipedal, reptilian-like creature with forest and rock features, along with stone scales covering its body. It carries a large "mountain range" with many peaks on its back, decorated with river patterns and waterfalls (which are, in fact, actual rivers and waterfalls) throughout its body, most visible on its torso peaks and shoulders. On its main peak, there is a rune vaguely resembling a four-pointed star. This "mountain range" extends down to Geortharoc's long tail, with foothills giving its tail a scaly, reptilian appearance. The Geortharoc has a small, reptilian head covered in "stone hairy scales," equipped with rocky tusks on its lower jaw that point upwards. Its rocky, scaly extremities end on sharp, pointed claws—three on its feet and four on its hands, with one of those four being a thumb. Geortharoc's chest presents a type of nucleus with what looks like debris around it. Males present a straight, sharp nose with forest details and small rock details around the chest. They are herbivores. These massive creatures are very rare to be seen as they're mostly hibernating somewhere for millions of years, though when the time is right they will awaken from their slumber to protect the delicate balance of nature with their titanic size.

entries.name: Ghalgeya
entries.content: The Ghalgeya appears to have long, bunny-like ears, with the head and body of a canine. It has long spines/frills along its chin, and short spines/frills along its ankles. The Ghalgeya also has a medium-length tail, which appears to have slits along the edges, and has "spikes" on each shoulder blade. It could be based on a hyena, even though the body shape appears to resemble a dingo. Males have three long whisker-like appendages on their chin, along with three spikes protruding from each shoulder. Females have spikes on their lower back. They are carnivores. Ghalgeya is a small and lean carnivore creature built for speeding underneath dense forest brush. Males wield long thick whiskers on their chins that emit pheromones for vital communication and are one of the few existing species on Sonaria where packs are led by patriarchs instead of matriarchs.

entries.name: Ghartokus
entries.content: The Ghartokus is a huge theropod partially resembling the Tyrannosaurus rex and some of the Wardens. It presents antlers that sport flowers and hanging draperies, and displays a huge flower on its back. The Ghartokus also has a build similar to that of advanced prehistoric theropods like the Tyrannosaurus, with small arms and heavy legs. Its neck and head fluff lead down to its belly. The Ghartokus has two rows of plates on the top of its body that stop when it reaches the hind legs, and its feet have a total of 5 toes on each foot, one of those toes being vestigial, resembling dewclaws which again, appear on theropod dinosaurs. On its bottom jaw are rocky-like patterns. The Ghartokus is decorated with these patterns, with some of them presenting spirals. These symbols appear on its small arms and the top of its hind legs. The blunt head shape also bears resemblance to some abelisaurids, such as the Carnotaurus or Majungasaurus (the closest one being Pycnonemosaurus). Males sport a fin-like structure located by the lower section of its back. Females display an extra flower at the end of its tail. They are carnivores. Brave and Strong, these creatures have prideful personalities. Ghartokus is an apex predator that primarily roams deep forest thicket to hunt for prey. Although a predator, these creatures are quite mellow and don't have a tendency to pick fights.

entries.name: Ghibli
entries.content: Ghibli is a sleek flying creature with a mechanical, aircraft-like appearance. It has two long and narrow segmented wings, in the middle of which there are two-clawed structures; the wings end in three short wing-tips. It has two engines mounted on its back. Near the base of the tail, the Ghibli sports twin ruddervators arranged in a V-shape, thin and triangular in form. Its tail features two more groups of fins, the first being a pair of short horizontal stabilisers; and lastly, on the very end, a full empennage of three fins, the vertical featuring a green decal. This creature has six uniquely shaped robotic legs, the middle pair being considerably thicker than the rest, and also being the only with two fingers instead of four. The legs are partially covered by a protruding rim. A pattern of green rectangles, resembling passenger aircraft windows, runs through the side of its body, beginning on the neck and ending somewhere around the start of the tail. Ghibli's head is similar to that of a shark's. It flaunts an iconic sharp-toothed grin reminiscent of fighter aircraft livery. The creature has three eyes, the third being significantly bigger and covering most of its forehead. It also has three pairs of mechanical "ears" on the sides of its head. The Ghibli's color palette consists of muted earthy tones, from chocolate brown to light sand, and some highlights of pistachio green. Males have a singular air intake-like structure protruding from their chest. They are carnivores. This creature inhabits the desert skies, relying on its large wings and winged tail for swift maneuvers. It ambushes prey from above, seizing them with four front arms before delivering a fatal drop.

entries.name: Gloracus
entries.content: The Gloracus is an armored quadrupedal creature with blue-green fins sprouting from its tail, legs, and head, along with finned front whiskers. It mostly consists of shades of brown with hints of beige and blue colors. Males have two extra whiskers on their snouts. Females have two extra fins protruding from the sides of their stomachs. They are herbivores. Gloracus form large herds for safety, often mingling with other herbivores. Generally gentle, they become agressive if threatened.

entries.name: Glovaucus
entries.content:
The Glovaucus is a quadrupedal creature with four main flipper-like appendages, the front of the two being larger than its hind flippers. Its body closely resembles that of a Blue Glaucus, having its overall shape as well as the creature's finned appendages. The Glovaucus's tail also has a finned end, resembling the aforementioned Blue Glaucus. More fin-like frills are present on its body, most noticeably in a set of three on both sides of its head. On top of its head, Glovaucus bears two sharp, triangular protrusions with thin, floating crystals behind them. On its head the Glovaucus has a row of spikes on each side, the same spikes being seen on its underside, below its neck, on its back and on the ridges of its wings. Its default palette consists of vibrant shades of orange and yellow, accompanied with darker brown and purples. Females have 2 shards floating above their horn, one short and one long. They are carnivores. Glovaucus are very aggressive towards other species. They prefer to swim in lava and hot springs where they hunt in packs of three. It is believed that these creatures are the ones responsible for Sonaria's volcanic eruptions.
- Glovaucus are very aggressive towards others that are not from their species.
- They prefer to swim in lava and hot springs instead of in actual water.
- They hunt in packs of 3.
- Females of this species are known as "material gworls", as they like shiny things and will hunt creatures if they have anything shiny like crystals and gold.
- Their favorite prey is Galeostra; they favor hunting them because they believe Galeostras to be inferior to them.
- When a Glovaucus eats a fruit they fall asleep immediately for some reason.
- They like to bully Minawiis as they love the effect of Necro Poison.

entries.name: Gnolrok
entries.content: The Gnolrok has a large torso, lacking hind legs, with a thick tail. Its body is made entirely of rock, with two enormous forearms and a small, pointed head with small, sharp teeth. Its mouth also contains a long, thin, milk-colored tongue. It has stone-like formations protruding from the back of its head, forearms, and the top of its tail tip that jut upward. It consists of a pale white, and a variety of light and pale browns, a dark gray, and light and dark greens. They also possess a singular, forward-mounted eye on their head, giving them a very threatening appearance that only grows worse with their size. Males have four spikes on their underbelly. Females lack the spikes that males have on their underbelly. They are herbivores. Gnolrok are large, lumbering golemn-like creatures. They lack any hind limbs, and traverse their stomping grounds with dense and heavy forearms coated in a thick layer of stone.

entries.name: Gobli
entries.content:
The Gobli is a small, winged creature about the size of a player's avatar. It has a pair of short and round wings on its back that are structured much like a bat's, having prominent beans at the end of each digit/'finger'. The Gobli also have arms that resemble its wings, with webbed fingers, though they are smaller and don't have as much webbing between them. It also has stumpy, tortoise-like hind legs and a large tail ending in a toe bean. Its head presents a pair of two-pointed-ears, a snout, a mouth with two pairs of slightly curved conical teeth and cartoon-y, large eyes with white sclera and a black iris and pupil. The Gobli's color palette consists of yellows, pink, white, black, and mainly various ombré shades of blue. Males possess a ridge of soft spikes on their neck, right below the chin. These squishy little goobers waddle around endlessly, looking for playmates. Its eyes are full of childish innocence, Goblis are extremely oblivious to any dangers that might be lurking. Usually these amphibians can befriend such predators... but on the rare occasion their charms fail... there can be dire consequences.
- Gobli will usually befriend their predators, albeit sometimes they fail at this (as said in description).
- They use their sticky sticky-pads (not only their feet) to climb on many surfaces and escape predators.
- They are said to be full of childish innocence.

entries.name: Golgaroth
entries.content: The Golgaroth is a quadrupedal artificial crocodilian creature with a large castle-like structure on its back. The largest of the structure's towers are connected by a bridge, and they all have multiple darkened windows containing blinking eyes. These also appear in similar fashion on the sides of its torso. These torso windows are surrounded by moss, which can also be found hanging on the neck and tail. The Golgaroth's head contains a split jaw, and the side of its neck is covered by thick armor, resembling a shingled roof of some sorts. Running down the neck and the back is a stone wall-like sail similar to that of spinosaurid dinosaurs. On its thick front legs and thinner back legs, the Golgaroth has an almost frilly sets of bricks that spread outwards to the side, as well as blue water-like patterns. Its tail has a similar overall shape to modern day crocodilians, but displayed with a stony texture and stone tablets lined up on top of it, each consecutive stone containing a different letter from the Sonarian Font which, when put together, spell "ruin." Males have some extra dark green moss hanging from the undersides of their necks. Females have two flags, one on each of their watchtowers. Golgaroth are humble crocodilian-like creatures. Don't be deceived by its lack of eyes on its head though, as it actually has multiple eyes throughout its body that can detect threats miles away.

entries.name: Gorgonichus
entries.content:
The Gorgonichus resembles a cross between a terror bird, a Dromaeosaurinae theropod, and a turkey with some vulture-like details on their neck plumage. As such, they are birds with generally muted and natural colors, typically brown, and a tail fan. The only distinctive differences are their raptor-like feet with five (5) fingers, and their mouth, which has a strange beak where its front resembles a row of retracted teeth fused together, resembling the pseudoteeth on some sea-birds. Additionally, their waddle is only present near the tip and sides of their beak. It is interesting to notice that unlike other Sonarian creatures at the moment of release, they have eyelids capable of blinking. Males have a pair of ram-like horns with a cuff on the left one, as well as an additional short protrusion on the top of their beaks that resembles a snood. Females have short fur on the top of their heads. Gorgonichus is a social creature that are often found in small groups. They aren't very bright and are extremely food motivated. They are very gluttonous and spend a majority of their time hunting and eating other creatures. Unfortunately for Gorgonichus, it is also very delicious itself.
- The Gorgonichus are comparable to very nippy chickens in their social circles, composed of packs of 4-6 with a pecking hierarchy order usually with the largest at the top.
- It is not uncommon for males to end up at the top just because their horns can make them appear bigger than they really are, but otherwise the gender of a Gorgonichus does not affect status.
- When Gorgonichus gather yearly for nesting, they usually shuffle up their groups upon leaving. Because of this, the pecking order has to be reestablished yearly, which causes lots of in-fighting.
- Gorgonichus are vicious with little strategy or reason when it comes to hunting down creatures, not even considering status effects they may inflict, and mostly just all rush in and start going ham, overwhelming creatures with numbers.
- Unless threatened by a significantly larger creature, they are very stubborn and don't stand down.
- Despite their aggressive nature both with other creatures and each other in close quarters, Gorgonichus don't mind other groups of their species and leave them be.
- They frequently mistake other avian creatures as the same species.
- Gorgonichus favor wooded biomes, but also can be found venturing in open grassy areas. They also migrate to the rockier regions of the desert annually to nest.

entries.name: Goskogur
entries.content: The Goskogur is a quadrupedal beast with a robust, gorilla-like build and a dark forest-green, brown, and crimson color palette. Its massive, muscular frame is covered in shaggy fur, interspersed with wooden, bark-like skin. Their deer-like skull mask is crowned with large, branching antlers and adorned with red, vibrant patterns. Sporting a set of sharp teeth, their mask features several horns on its lower jaw. Behind their mask, they hide their true, flat gorilla-like face. Their forelimbs are long and powerful, ending in five clawed fingers. The shorter hind legs are equally strong, supporting its heavy frame, with two toes on each foot. Males possess longer and large chest fur, which extends from their chin to their lower abdomen. They are omnivores. The Goskogur is a mysterious and powerful beast, primarily found in the forests and swamps of Sonaria. Although terrifying in appearance, they primarily feed on fruits and scavenged meat. Their wooden covering evolved to mimic the decaying skulls of common Sonarian predators, it serves as a warning to what may become of any predator that picks a fight with a Goskogur.

entries.name: Gramoss
entries.content: The Gramoss is a large quadrupedal, gargoyle-like creature with a sturdy build and small, flightless wings made of stick-like appendages and stone-like feathers. Its body is primarily light grey with a brown, wood-like underside. Its sleek, somewhat elongated head has moss draping down to its eye area and two mammoth-like tusks extending from the back of the jaw. Two very short tusk-like structures extend down from where its eyes should be, and another structure, resembling a snood, hangs from the forehead on both sides. Four upright plates adorn its neck, while its back and long tail are layered with large plates fanning outwards. The plates break apart into smaller pieces near the tail tip, exposing its wood-like appearance with some branch-like protrusions. The tail tip has moss/leaf-like structures and small upright plates. Moss covers its tusks, neck, back, shoulders, thighs, tail, and upper section of the wings. Sharp quill-like spikes protrude from the moss and plates on its back and tail. The top of Gramoss' hind legs rise higher than its hips. Its thighs feature glowing white patches and five small circular plates. Flat plates stick out behind each leg, and it has four pointy nails on the front legs and three on the back. Glowing white runes adorn its shoulders, upper wings, and the last upright plate on the tail, emitting rune-like symbols. Males have an extra upright plate with a glowing white rune on top their heads. Females have four twigs protruding between their neck plates and lack the head plate that males have. They are herbivores. Gramoss are surprisingly docile and social herbivores with the capacity to empathize for other creatures. They are commonly seen sheltering smaller creatures beneath its stone-like body as it grazes for food.

entries.name: Grysallmog
entries.content: The Grysallmog is a large hexapedal creature, having four main legs as well as two smaller appendages located underneath its head. It has six eyes, three on each side of its head. Its body is covered in many leaves that resemble carrot tops, most notably spanning from behind its neck all the way down to its 'tail', which wholly consists of the leaves. Underneath its leaves, the Grysallmog bears a scaly body and an underside coated with thick tufts of fur. All of its limbs, including its two arms, end in scaly, clawed appendages. Its legs bear an orange, root-like 'frill' that can also be seen covering most of the creature's face. The Grysallmog also has a prominent frilled nose resembling that of a star-nosed mole. Its default colours consist of dull yellow-orange, earthy browns, shades of muted green, and a pop of bright orange. Males have a large frilled nose at the front of their heads. Females have a smaller frilled nose at the front of their heads. They are photocarnivores, meaning they eat meat and don't need water to survive. Gryllsamog are large mole-like creatures with an insect-like build. They ravage burrows and then sunbathe to collect sunlight needed to break down their food.

entries.name: Gryvila
entries.content:
The Gryvila appears to have a salamander-like body plan with wings adorning its back, and an extra pair of smaller wings near its hip. It has large web-like fans on its head and whiskers coming from its chin. Its tail is long and large with a wide fan. On the tips of its wing and over its tail are floating bubbles/raindrops. Its colors are vibrant and resemble those of tropical fish. Males have two whiskers on their chin and two large tail fins above their tail-tip. Females have two extra fins at the top of their head and fins on each of their legs. They are herbivores. Gryvila are docile and sociable semi-aquatic creatures. Their bodies are coated in a thin layer of poisonous slippery oil which allow them to glide through warm bodies of water effortlessly. They wield very vibrant colours, which signify they inhabit tropical coral reefs and are not safe to touch.
- Gryvila are able to see in ultra-violet light, allowing them to view the world's hidden vibrance, similar to real-life birds and bees.

entries.name: Gurava
entries.content: The Gurava is a quadrupedal, frog-like creature that consists of mainly green shades. On the top of its head, it has what resembles a wizard hat, though it does not appear to be attached to the creature. It also has a "cloak" covering the topside of its body that consists of several frills/ruffles. It has a short, stubby, seemingly layered tail. While its colors are primarily of green shades, the Gurava's underbelly is a bluer teal color with an adornment of yellow and red ornaments. Swirly, polka dotted, and even heart shapes can be found on parts of its cloak, hat, and body. Its back legs are much longer than the front legs when stretched out. Males have round earmuff-like buttons covering their possible ear emplacements. Females have a round pearl-like protrusion on the base of their necks. They are omnivores. These creatures are usually solitary but may form small groups of up to three members, particularly in old age. Primarily nocturnal, they consume fireflies, resembling living lanterns. They lure lost creatures deeper into the swamp before vanishing, leaving them disoriented and stranded.

entries.name: Hellion Warden
entries.content:
The Hellion Warden appears to be a quadrupedal creature, having four (4) legs but a large arm-like structure between them. It has an elongated, crested head with 3 pairs of hollow eyes. The markings on its face curl outwards and curve to face the front of the creature. Its body appears to be covered in layers of scale/armor, which become most prominent on its tail, which has a small mouth at the end. Bright spots can be seen around the edges of its armor and along the tail, and glowing bits can be seen floating around its body. It appears to have a mask floating in front of its head. The tip of its tail is orange and resembles a pair of jaws. Females have a feature which seems to be a gear, which hovers above their backs. They are carnivores. The Hellion Warden is elusive and sly, and more docile than commonly thought to be, often lurking in the dark to strike fear into other creatures' eyes. Ancient creatures of old would call them Nukzeh, often giving gifts and offerings in return for protection by Hellion.
- Hellion Wardens are very good parents, to the point to where they would rather starve than leave their children.
- Hellion Wardens have fur, but it's similar to velvet and glows in the winter.

entries.name: Imeaorn
entries.content:
The Imeaorn is a bipedal creature. Its two massive, pillar-like forelimbs end in backward facing claws. Smaller arms protrude from where the forelimbs meet the abdomen. Its incredibly long jaw almost seems to extend into its own neck, while its two sets of eyes sit on the tip of the head. The marking on its face somewhat resembles a skull or mask. Various flaps and spikes span the length of the Imeaorns' body, particularly on its neck and tail. Additional striped markings decorate the flaps as well as the legs and neck. Males present fin-like appendages on their heads and similar spikes under their tail. Females have additional fin-like appendages to the sides of their neck and on their ankles. They are omnivores. The Imeaorn is a large omnivore that dwells in shadow. Its legs take up the majority of its body mass, allowing it to make long, powerful strides. The Imeaorn's unique anatomy is entirely built for swiftness and speed.
- Imeaorn will stalk other creatures when it's younger to build up its hunting skills. Alongside this, Imeaorn parents will also build up a tower of snow or stone and let their children attack it to gain confidence in fighting.

entries.name: Imini
entries.content: Imini is a small creature that resembles a hermit crab, having six limbs in total and a shell covering its abdomen, as well as two eyestalks. It has a s'more-themed design with marshmallows scattered across the top of it, markings on its upper body that resemble melted chocolate, and two sticks of chocolate protruding from its shell. Females have two additional sticks of chocolate on their necks. They are herbivores. These bite-sized creatures thrive on beaches and in shallow waters, eating whatever wanders into their path.

entries.name: Iztajuatl
entries.content:
The Iztajuatl is a fiery, multi-eyed, somewhat lizard-like creature with a glowing sword embedded into its forehead and several glowing joints and magma-themed decorations. Many weapons stick out of its back and tail tip, such as axes, spears, and knives. The back of its neck produces smoke and it also possesses an axe-shaped tail. The Iztajuatl also has multiple eye-like decorations on its limbs, body, and tail. Tusks and blades protrude from its mouth and lower jaw. Its neck and tail are decorated by multiple rock-like spines. They are carnivores. This hot tempered creature is a testament to strength and resilience, along its body lie the weapons once used in an attempt to eradicate it from this world. Solitary in nature, the Iztajuatl appears particularly fond of scorching hot territories.
- Iztajuatl MUST live near volcanic areas, especially babies and male Iztajuatls.
- Iztajuatls are a primarily all-female pack-based species.
- Females tend to disregard or outcast any males.
- Male Iztajuatl CAN NOT and DO NOT "RULE" a pack.
- Since there are more females than males, Iztajuatl females can choose to pair with another female or be solitary.
- Female Iztajuatls have "no maternal instincts whatsoever. Forget them kids".

entries.name: Jabblebashhe
entries.content:
The Jabblebashhe is characterized by its bipedal form, which consists of a long body with two slender limbs. The skin of the creature is covered in melted ice cream-like markings, which can be seen down the neck and chest as well as on the top of the head. The head and neck are adorned with three pairs of large, candle-like horns, each of which is tipped with a "wick" from which pink flames are emitting form. The back of the creature protrudes from three waffle cone-shaped structures, all of which are adorned with similar flames. The Jabblebashhe features a single, unipupilled eye at the center of the face, as well as a wide mouth with sharp teeth and a striped tongue. Males have two horns protruding from the back of their jaw. They are carnivores. A dessert straight from the depths of the underworld, Jabblebashhe constantly craves flesh and bone. These creatures produce intense heat from deep inside their body, making their skin boil on the outside. Jabblebashhe's skin is useful in battle, being hard to penetrate and able to severely burn attackers. 
- Jabblebashhe is a ferocious foe that constantly craves flesh to sustain its undying hunger. This hunger is caused by its unfortunate trait of ever-melting and boiling skin. If Jabblebashhe ever consumes a creature, that creature's flesh will be melted down and used to create a new layer of "ice cream".
- This constant melting is the cause of its skinny appearance.
- Jabblebashhe's skin can start to nearly harden under freezing temperatures, slowing the speed at which flesh drips off of its body. Because of this, although extremely unlikely, Jabblebashhe could gain considerable weight by consuming creatures in these conditions, and lose its usual skinny appearance.
- As it runs the risk of becoming too hot for its own good, Jabblebashhe is able to let out a stream of flames. This can lower its rising temperature and avoid certain death.

entries.name: Kretśnik
entries.content:
Kretśnik is a stout, quadrupedal creature designed after pancakes. The creature has a heavy build, with a thick neck, legs, tail, and a block-shaped head which lacks any visible eyes. Several pancake-shaped flaps cover its body, notably its shoulders, thighs, and tail, with the largest being draped over its head and back (resembling the mantle of a slug). Its feet are four-toed and paw-like in appearance, featuring long, curved claws, and an additional thumb on its front feet exclusively. Kretśnik has two mouths — one on its head, and one on its tail — which both feature short downwards-pointing teeth and a pair of long tusks that jut upwards. It also features a striped patterning across its body that resembles dripping syrup, which is most prominent on its tail, but also appears on the sides of its underbelly and near its mouths. On both mouths, the "syrup" extends into whisker-like growths, which appear in rows of three on each end. Kretśnik's design also includes several toppings: dollops of whipped cream appear on its head and legs, there are thinly-cut strawberries on its chest and tail, and whole blueberries and sliced bananas line its sides. By default, Kretśnik is several shades of golden brown and cream, with dark brown syrup, blue blueberries, and red strawberries. Female Kretśnik have a pat of butter on their back. They are carnivores. Found in dark caves and burrows, the Kretsnik are extremely sluggish creatures who spend most of their time lazing around. These blind, mole-like burrowers hypnotize and entrance prey with their pungent smell which can cause hallucinations.
- Kretśnik are blind, mole-like burrowers which can be found underground in dark caves, or burrows of their own.
- While Kretśnik are sluggish creatures that spend most of their time lazing about, they produce a sweet, intoxicating smell that can hypnotize and entrance prey, meaning that a Kretśnik does not need to tread far to hunt. Prolonged exposure at a short distance can cause hallucinations.
- A Kretśnik pack can create such a strong aroma that they can be smelt from miles away.
- As semi-social creatures, the Kretśnik tolerate one another, but when they do get into a dispute, they will enter a fighting ritual. Most often, the sweeter, more intoxicating-smelling Kretśnik will win.
- As mean as they may seem, the Kretśnik are actually very sweet towards those who are kind to it, having a distinct sense of empathy.
- Baby Kretśnik are particularly soft blobs with legs and two heads. Often hiding beneath an adult’s shedded pancake, the baby Kretśnik stays protected and hidden.

entries.name: Korathos
entries.content: The Korathos walks on two sturdy legs, and has a broad yet muscular looking torso that is set in a hunched stance and is dark in color. Near the base of the split tail lie various curved and crooked growths with the tail splitting in two, a red stripe flowing down to the tips on the inside of both tails. It has two long arms with hands that have three fingers on each. On its neck are spike-like growths and at the head it has nine gleaming white eyes with no pupils in each of them along with a mouth of sharp teeth. Near the base of its bottom jaw are four long tentacles with uniquely shaped appendages at the end of them with multiple spots similar to Korathos' eyes in each of them, the tail having those same appendages at the ends of them. The feet are in a position similar to various birds of prey, having the middle part of each toe bent inward to support its massive body. Males have multiple large spikes on their back that have a thin glowing pattern to them. Females have a pair of dorsal fins on their back that lack the glowing pattern. They are carnivores. Korathos are massive, ruthless hunters of the night that utilize their dark coloration to remain undetected. The frilly plates along their neck and tail can pick up vibrations and can be shaken to create an ominous rattling sound. Korathos have a cold intelligence to them and often seek to taunt other creatures.

entries.name: Militrua
entries.content:
Militrua is a large, hexapodal creature that resembles crustaceans and beetles. It has a spiny blue exoskeleton and a lengthy tail. Its exoskeleton is adorned with bioluminescent speckles present in either the form of rings or dots, and it has a horn protruding from its carapace. The Militrua also appears to have an electrical current running from the floating gem above its head to the gem on its tail-base. Males have spike-like protrusions on their tails. Females lack aforementioned protrusions. They are herbivores. Militrua is an extremely defensive herbivore that dwells on the ocean floor around shallow bays. Its shell is made entirely of metal, making it an extremely durable creature. Electric currents run through its shell at all times that shock predators when they are attacked.
- These large herbivores are extremely docile, and spend almost no time attacking anything but smaller carnivores that can reach under their shell.
- Large carnivores tend to not attack Militrua, as its shell is made purely of metal that runs electric currents through its entire shell. Most predators die before they can get past the shell. Small predators however, take down sick and baby Militrua by slowly biting their legs until they can't walk anymore.
- Militrua gather in herds of thousands to migrate across the lands, but usually spend most their time at the deep sea, only coming up for oxygen.
- Militrua are not the best at handling their babies, but do protect them when necessary with their large tail spikes.
- Militrua conducts a special type of electricity using little microscopic crystals in its electric sacs that rub together to charge the creature.

entries.name: Minawii
entries.content: The Minawii is a small, grub-like hexapedal creature. It has two fuzzy antennae and moss growing on its back, which foster small mushrooms. Its back is relatively armored, covered in a thick, shell-like material. Its tail is thick and ends with a large bulb-like structure, similar to the abdomen of a firefly. They are omnivores. The Minawii is a creature that's shy and timid. They hide in deep oceans where they call cold coral reefs their home. Whenever they see creatures approaching them, they will swim away as fast as possible.

entries.name: Momola
entries.content: The Momola is a slim, bipedal creature that resembles a monarch butterfly. It has two pairs of arms which have circular markings on them, as well as the thighs and back. It also has spikes protruding from its legs. Armored plates and antennae cover its head, and thin, feather-like red and yellow spines decorate its neck. Its body shows many circular and diamond-shaped markings, and has a plump tail that looks like an insect abdomen. Males have more feather-like spines on their backs. Females have frills on their arms. They are herbivores. A flying herbivore with bright patterns and unique patterns. Momola typically travel in large flocks and aren't aggressive whatsoever. Though they do lack strength they are quick and wont have a hard time escaping if threatened.

entries.name: Novus Warden
entries.content:
The Novus Warden is a hexapodal, rocky shrimp-like creature covered in armor, spikes, and intricate patterns with no seen eyes. Its limbs are formed of floating rock interconnected by a bright static flux slightly resembling clouds and with a spiral pattern on each one, and its tail is decorated by floating pebbles. The same spiral pattern can be seen engraved into the armor on its tail-base. Its head features a long, curved snout and its neck has layers of armor similar to that of a crustacean. At the base of its tail, two prominent blade-like protrusions can be seen. Like other Wardens, it dons a mask-like ornament which levitates above its head. Its mask appears to resemble leaves and shrimp-tails. Females have curved, ram-like horns behind their jaws. They are omnivores. This warden's appearance marks the start of fresh life, but hardly spotted as it is able to traverse the land, skies and seas. The Novus Warden is a large, majestic beast bound by its incredible life force and magic, so strong its aura sometimes helps the elements around it to flourish.
- The Novus Warden has the same intelligence levels as the other wardens, usually staying underwater. Solitary, but many creatures like to surround it due to the positive natural aura it emits.
- It does not have eyes and instead uses its extremely long protrusions to ‘see’ the world around it.
- The Novus Warden is usually found alone, passive most of the time, and only attacks if it faces a real threat.
- The Novus Warden usually enjoys floating in the water as it uses up less of its magic.
Sometimes stranded creatures in the middle of the sea find themselves being carried to shore by the Novus Warden.
- The Novus Warden is a species capable of feeling emotion. Their aura changes completely when in a bad temper, making those too close to it feel uneasy.
- The Novus Warden can laugh.
- No one knows how long this Warden has existed.

entries.name: Pierry
entries.content:
The Pierry is a bipedal creature with an overall cherry pie theme. It has a wedge-shaped head, similar to that of a slice of pie, with openings on the side revealing a cherry-sludge. On its head it bears decorations similar to that of a cowboy hat, with what appears to be dollops of whipped cream making up the crown of the hat. There are also two cherries situated on top of its "hat." Along its neck and back are two rows of triangular ridges which stop at the creature's rump. Along the sides of its neck and torso are slits which leak and reveal more of the cherry-sludge within the creature, like the slits one might see on a pie. Its tail is disconnected from its body and seems to be made of the same cherry-sludge which leaks from its body, and the tail ends with a large four-fingered hand. Its arms are similar, being disconnected from its body, being made of cherry-sludge, and having four fingers. Males have multiple green ferns floating near the hands. Females have extra cherry sludge leaking from the gap made by the tail. They are carnivores. These speedy little fellas are extreme opportunists. They can be found pestering local creatures, taking the chance to steal any food from them; even if it looks horribly inedible.
- Pierry will sometimes work together in robbing other creatures of their meals. Once the meal is acquired, they will then fight each other for it.
- Pierry pick on larger creatures since they can outrun/outmaneuver them.
- Because of their high impulsiveness and low intelligence, Pierry often find themselves in sticky situations.
- Pierry will eat anything even if it doesn't seem edible.
- The Pierry uses the large hand on its tail to transport portions of food that they would not be able to carry with their front arms.

entries.name: Raiquazok
entries.content: The Raiquazok heavily represents the male MUTO (Massive Unidentified Terrestrial Organism) from the Godzilla (2014) film, having long, somewhat triangular, rigid wings. These wings separate two-thirds of the way through to reveal two hook-like spikes at the tip of the wings. It also has a long "thumb" with a barbed hook at the end. Its head represents the well-known "MUTO" head, being rigid and having beak-like additions. It has spikes under its chin and elbow, with their front legs' "toes" being long and hooked, similar to the ones of a MUTO. Their hind toes resemble those of a Lus-Adarch, except they have the same barbed claws. They have a pair of "wings" similar to the ones of a swallowtail butterfly (Having extensions coming off it) as the tail, and another, larger, spikier pair above it, next to the wing. Males have a golden addition to the spikes under their chin and elbow, making it look bigger and more decorative. Females lack this golden addition and only have black spikes under the chin and on their elbow. Raiquazok's mighty wings cast a shadow over the inhabitants of Sonaria. Its fiery colors a warning to all of its fearsome nature.

entries.name: Reviiaton
entries.content: The Reviiaton is a leviathan-like creature with a quadrupedal-like and slim build, having clawed flippers on its front pair of limbs and clawless ventral flippers on its hind limbs, and sporting a long dorsal fin that stems from the base of the neck and continues to the horizontal caudal fin. All their fins have a look halfway between being complex ray-fins and being made of feathers. Reviiaton have additional features such as a large backwards-pointing horn on the tip of their snout, baubles which grow from the top of their torso, and several white spots covering the sides of their bodies and neck. Their streamlined body is made for darting out of the water to catch flying prey or to propel them in the depths. Males have an additional dorsal neck fin. Females have two ear fins that look like an extra fin collar near the base of their heads. They are carnivores. Reviiaton is a very fast swimmer, but with little defense due to the fact that there is nothing to protect it in its body. Its way of attacking is encircling its attacker with its swift speed to confuse it.

entries.name: Ripirin
entries.content: The Ripirin is a skeletal hexapod creature with a floating orb on its tail and its head. Four horns protrude from its head, and several vertebrae extensions stem from its spinal chord. Both pairs of legs present long claws. They are carnivores. Ripirin feed on the souls of innocent and sinful creatures, which they also use to create dangerous magic. The air turns cold around them and other creatures shiver in their presence. They have light green blood.

entries.name: Vahiaex
entries.content: The Vahiaex is a bulky hexapedal creature, sporting a dark coloration of blacks, dark greys, and bioluminescent patterns across its body giving a dull green hue. This creature possesses a maw filled with sharp pointed teeth, with the back two fangs appearing almost tusk-like, and in its glowing jaws hold a secondary pair of small jaws that have teeth-like serrations lining outside the mouth. The head is aligned with short horn-like frills, with 2 sets of whiskers at the creature's cheeks. The Vahiaex's legs are stout and muscular for walking and running, with each leg holding four clawed toes, one of them curving upwards. Its arms are long, with large 'hands' at the end of them. Its tail is medium in length and bears spikes at its tip. Females have an extra pair of whiskers on their jaw. They are carnivores. Raiquazok's mighty wings cast a shadow over the inhabitants of Sonaria. Its fiery colors a warning to all of its fearsome nature.

entries.name: Verdant Warden
entries.content:
The Verdant Warden is a slender creature bearing 4 legs and 2 arms (6 limbs total), giving it a centaur-like look. It has a slim, rabbit-like face with long ears and flowering antlers, as well as fur on the back of its neck. Its forearms have long tufts of fur that drape downward. It has a short, rabbit-like tail. Petal-like markings and swirls can be found over its shoulders and lower body. Males have additional segments on their antlers. Females have longer fur on the back of their neck. They are herbivores. The Verdant Warden is rumored to be the embodiment of spring itself, and sometimes referred to as Farhaus. It's a peaceful creature that is usually seen during the flowering seasons. Due to it's friendliness it is often seen with other small critters and birds. The Warden naturally inhabits the flower cove and plains biomes.
- Verdant Warden is also called Farhaus - Sentinel of Life and Bringer of Spring.

entries.name: Xenolif
entries.content: The Xenolif is a gangly, hexapedal creature. Only four of its limbs, all of which feature four digits, are used in locomotion, whereas its forelimbs are used exclusively for utility and are held above the ground. Two-pronged horns sprout from the back of its head, and a third larger one protrudes from its nose. The Xenolif also possesses four free-moving antennae/whisker-like structures, with one pair extending from its mandible and the other from its hips. Its eyes, which glow, feature two pairs of long, horizontal pupils which gives the Xenolif a four-eyed appearance despite having a single pair. A thin crest runs down its neck and back, and its tail ends in a sharp point reminiscent of a barbed hook. The whole creature's body features a prominent striped pattern. Xenolif is purple, grey, black, and magenta. Males have an additional three spiked-tuft protruding from their second forelimb set's axilla. They are carnivores. Xenolif are odd looking creatures unrecognized by most of Sonarian life, referred mostly by their invasive nature of their species. They are somewhat pesky, stealing prey and killing wildlife pivotal to other creatures environments. They flourish in small colonies, communicating long-distance to each other both to hunt and to warn others.

entries.name: Yenyasha
entries.content:
Yenyashas are quadrupedal sheep-like creatures. Fluffy clouds span across the creature, from its fleecy legs to its wavy tail. These creatures have a thin, purple cloth that is dressed over their hind legs to the end of their torso and over their neck. They have wavy blue hair that covers their eyes and cloud-covered antennae. Yenyashas have patterns all over their body structure, including their clouds. Light blue markings and growths on their cheeks resemble dripping tears. Females have raindrop-shaped growths on their chins that dangle from side-to-side. They are herbivores. Yenyashas are shy creatures, typically lurking in places where nobody else is there. They adore the rain and those wet seasons are the time they feel an ounce of peace and tranquility. The days it is very foggy, their cloudy fur allows them to blend into their surroundings, allowing themselves to be better hidden from others.
- During clear nights with full moons, Yenyashas like to gather under the moonlight and gaze upon it. Typically, this happens near shores where the tides have risen.
- Yenyashas tend to have severe paranoia.
- Very rarely do they have the confidence to have contact with the other creatures.
- The most common cause of death for Yenyashas is being caught whilst hiding or getting so depressed when there's no rain it dies.
- Yenyashas do indeed have eyes, but they are obscured most of the time.
- The jewels on a Yenyasha's antennae are real minerals that they find during their journey of growing up.
- It is said that the cloudy fur of a Yenyasha is so soft and light that touching it feels like dipping your hand into cool water.
